mainTopic: How much of a year counts as a year for planting (רבי מאיר vs. רבי אלעזר), their source in the פסוק about נח, and whether the world was created in ניסן or תשרי.
overview: A ברייתא teaches that a tree planted thirty days before ראש השנה counts as having had a year. The גמרא asks whose view this follows. רבי מאיר seems not to fit, since he counts even one day as a year. רבי אלעזר does not fit either: a משנה in שביעית and רב נחמן's rule show that he would need rooting time plus thirty more days. So the גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is רבי מאיר, and its thirty days are rooting time. The thirtieth day counts both as the last rooting day and as the one day of the year. רבי יוחנן then shows that both תנאים learn their rule from the same פסוק about נח: רבי מאיר from the word 'year', and רבי אלעזר from 'the first month'. The גמרא infers that both hold the world was created in ניסן. It then brings a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר says the world was created in תשרי, along with other events in תשרי and on ראש השנה. That ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If one day counts at the end of a year, it should count at the start too
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of a challenge against saying the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר: by his own logic, one day at the beginning of the year should be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it logical that one day should also count as a year at the beginning?
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a challenge that began earlier. The גמרא argues that if רבי מאיר counts one day as a full year, then one day should be enough here too, and the ברייתא should not need thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a single day at the end of a year counts as a whole year. The גמרא reasons with a קל וחומר: if one day counts at the end, it should certainly count at the beginning. That clashes with the ברייתא's requirement of thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is it not logical?' A formula that introduces a קַל וָחוֹמֶר.
Counts (literally 'goes up'), meaning it counts toward the total.
At its beginning, meaning the start of the year.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It finishes a sentence earlier, which began roughly: 'If רבי מאיר says one day at the end of the year counts as a year...'

phrases.english: is it not logical that one day
phrases.notes: This wraps up the קל וחומר that started a bit earlier.

phrases.english: should count at its beginning?
phrases.notes: At the start of the year, as opposed to the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיּוֹם אֶחָד עוֹלֶה בִּתְחִלָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge begun on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one day counts as a year at the end of a year, then by קל וחומר it should count at the beginning. So רבי מאיר would not need thirty days.

steps.title: Trying רבי אלעזר instead: he would need sixty days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes רבי אלעזר as the author but immediately objects that he would require thirty days plus thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what? Does it follow רבי אלעזר? Then thirty and thirty are needed!
steps.whatsHappening: Having pushed רבי מאיר aside, the גמרא tries רבי אלעזר as the author of the ברייתא. It immediately challenges this too: by his view you would need thirty plus thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that thirty days in a year count as a year. But a planting also needs time to take root before the counting can begin. So by his view you would need thirty days to root and another thirty to count as a year, which is more than the ברייתא's thirty.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, what [will you say]?' Introduces the alternative option, usually to reject it.

phrases.english: Rather, what? Is it Rabbi Elazar?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is suggesting that maybe רבי אלעזר is the one behind this teaching instead.

phrases.english: He would need thirty and thirty!
phrases.notes: Thirty days to take root plus thirty days to count as a year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since רבי מאיר seemed not to fit, the גמרא tries a different author and challenges that too.
steps.kashyaTarget: Assigning the ברייתא to רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר requires thirty days for rooting and thirty days to count as a year. The ברייתא only says thirty.

steps.title: משנה source: רבי אלעזר requires thirty days for rooting
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in שביעית shows that רבי אלעזר forbids planting less than thirty days before the שמיטה year, because the planting needs thirty days to take root.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: One may not plant, layer, or graft on the eve of שביעית less than thirty days before ראש השנה. If he did plant, layer, or graft, he must uproot it. These are the words of רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove that רבי אלעזר requires thirty days just for a planting to take root.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Planting within thirty days of the שמיטה year is forbidden because the rooting would happen during שביעית itself. This shows that, for רבי אלעזר, rooting alone takes thirty days. So he would need another thirty for the year count, giving sixty in total.

keyTerms.meaning: Layering: bending a branch into the ground so it roots.
Grafting a branch onto another tree.
The year before the שְׁמִיטָּה year.

phrases.english: As we learned: one may not plant, and one may not layer,
phrases.notes: Opening of the משנה in שביעית.

phrases.english: and one may not graft on the eve of the Sabbatical year
phrases.notes: Three methods of starting a plant.

phrases.aramaic: פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: less than thirty days before Rosh Hashanah,
phrases.notes: Otherwise the rooting would happen in שביעית.

phrases.english: and if he planted, layered, or grafted, he must uproot it,
these are the words of Rabbi Elazar.
phrases.notes: So for רבי אלעזר, taking root takes thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the 'thirty and thirty' challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר requires thirty days for rooting alone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת שביעית about planting before the שמיטה year.

steps.title: Other opinions on rooting time: three days or two weeks
steps.stepSummary: The same משנה continues: רבי יהודה says grafting roots within three days, and רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say two weeks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Any grafting that does not take root within three days will not take root anymore. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: two weeks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה, which records other views on how long a planting takes to root. These views prepare the ground for רב נחמן's rule in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three opinions on rooting time: thirty days, three days, and two weeks. The next step will show that, whichever opinion you take, you still add thirty days for the year count.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: Second opinion in the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַרְכָּבָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ קוֹלֶטֶת בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים —
phrases.english: any graft that does not take root within three days
will no longer take root.
phrases.notes: So rooting takes only three days.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
phrases.notes: Third opinion.

phrases.english: two weeks.
phrases.notes: Rooting takes two weeks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The range of opinions on how long rooting takes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rest of the משנה in שביעית.

steps.title: רב נחמן: always add thirty days on top of rooting time
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה rules that every opinion needs its rooting time plus thirty days for the year to count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: According to the one who says thirty, you need thirty and thirty. According to the one who says three, you need three and thirty. According to the one who says two weeks, you need two weeks and thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an אמורא's rule that the thirty days counted as a year are always added on top of the rooting time. This confirms the challenge against רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rooting time and year-count time are two separate periods that do not overlap. So for רבי אלעזר the total is sixty days. That does not match the ברייתא's thirty.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says.

steps.whyThisMatters: It establishes the principle that rooting time is separate from, and added before, the thirty days that count as a year. The whole סוגיא depends on this.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
according to the one who says thirty,
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: it requires thirty and thirty;
phrases.notes: Thirty to root plus thirty to count as a year.

phrases.english: according to the one who says three,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: it requires three and thirty;
phrases.notes: Thirty-three days.

phrases.english: according to the one who says two weeks,
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: it requires two weeks and thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the opinions in the משנה to the year-count question.
steps.raayaObject: That rooting time and the thirty days are added together, so רבי אלעזר needs sixty.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה.

steps.title: Even רבי יהודה would need thirty-three days
steps.stepSummary: Even if the author held like רבי יהודה's short rooting time, he would still need thirty-three days, not thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if he holds like רבי יהודה, he needs three and thirty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes off a possible escape route. Even with the shortest rooting time, רבי יהודה's three days, the total would be thirty-three days, not thirty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might suggest that the author holds רבי אלעזר's thirty-day year with רבי יהודה's quick rooting. Even then, three days plus thirty does not equal thirty. So no version of the 'thirty days count as a year' view explains the ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי נָמֵי, כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ —
phrases.english: and even if he holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: Trying the shortest rooting time.

phrases.english: he needs three and thirty!
phrases.notes: Thirty-three days, still not thirty.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי נָמֵי, כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the challenge to block a possible way out.
steps.kashyaTarget: Any attempt to fit the ברייתא to the 'thirty days count as a year' view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even the shortest rooting time plus thirty days comes to more than thirty.

steps.title: It really is רבי מאיר, and the thirty days are for rooting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר. Its thirty days are the time needed for the planting to take root, not the year count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it really is רבי מאיר, and when it says thirty, it means for taking root.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its first suggestion, רבי מאיר, and answers the original challenge from step 1. The thirty days in the ברייתא are not for counting a year. They are the time the planting needs to take root.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 1 assumed that the thirty days were about the year count. In fact they are rooting time. Once the tree has rooted, רבי מאיר's rule that even a tiny part of the year counts as a year takes over, so no extra thirty days are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Really, actually.' Returns to the original position.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר. The thirty days are rooting time, and after rooting, even a tiny part of the year counts as a full year. רבי אלעזר is rejected because he would need rooting time plus thirty more days.
steps.confusionAlert: The two 'thirties' are different things. One is how long the planting takes to root. The other is how many days count as a year. The whole answer depends on telling them apart.

phrases.english: Rather, it really is Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: Back to the first suggestion.

phrases.english: and when it says thirty, it is for taking root.
phrases.notes: Answers the challenge from step 1.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the רבי אלעזר path blocked, the גמרא returns to רבי מאיר and reinterprets the thirty days.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting what the number in the ברייתא refers to.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The thirty days in the ברייתא were assumed to be the time that counts as a year, which clashes with רבי מאיר's one-day rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The thirty days are rooting time. After that, רבי מאיר's rule that one day counts as a year applies.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, and its thirty days refer to the time needed for rooting.

steps.title: Shouldn't it be thirty-one days?
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, you need thirty days for rooting plus one day for the year, so thirty-one days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should need thirty-one days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 7. It says the math does not add up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, one day in a year counts as a full year. The ברייתא needs thirty days for the planting to take root, and then one more day, still before ראש השנה, so that the rooted tree has a day in the planting year that counts as a year. That makes thirty-one, but the ברייתא only says thirty.

phrases.english: If so,
he should require thirty-one days!
phrases.notes: Thirty days for rooting, plus one day to count as a year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the math of the answer in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 7 that, according to רבי מאיר, the ברייתא's thirty days are for rooting (לִקְלִיטָה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Thirty rooting days plus one day for the year equals thirty-one, not thirty.

steps.title: The thirtieth day counts for both
steps.stepSummary: The thirtieth day counts both as the last rooting day and as the one day in the new year.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that the thirtieth day counts for this and for that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. One single day can do two jobs at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thirtieth day, the last day before ראש השנה, finishes the thirty days of rooting. At the same time, it serves as the one day of the planting year that makes that year count as a year. So thirty days are enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Counts for here and for there (counts twice)

phrases.english: He holds:
the thirtieth day counts for here and for there.
phrases.notes: It counts toward rooting and toward the year.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָבַר: יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים עוֹלֶה לְכָאן וּלְכָאן
steps.terutzResolutionType: One day counts toward both requirements.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rooting days and the year-day must be separate days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The thirtieth day serves both purposes, so thirty days are enough.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר. Day 30 counts both as the last rooting day and as the one day in the planting year that makes that year count as a year.

steps.title: Both opinions learn from the same verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר both learn their rule from the פסוק about the drying of the earth after the מבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both of them learned from one verse: "And it was in the one and six hundredth year, in the first month, on the first of the month."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings the source verse that both opinions use. This sets up the next steps, where each one's reading will be explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument about how much of a year counts as a year is not a guess. Both תנאים build their view from the same פסוק in בראשית (8:13). They just read it differently.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
And both of them expounded one verse:
"And it was in the one and six hundredth year,
phrases.notes: בראשית 8:13, when the waters dried up after the מבול.

phrases.english: in the first month, on the first of the month"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וּשְׁנֵיהֶן מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא to the source in the פסוק behind רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר both derive their view from בראשית 8:13.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: one day counts as a year
steps.stepSummary: On the very first day of the new year, the פסוק already calls it the 601st year. So one day in a year counts as a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: Since only one day had entered the year, and the verse already calls it a year, learn from this that one day in a year counts as a year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי מאיר reads the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It was only the first day of the first month, yet the תורה already calls it the 601st year. So just one day into a year is enough to count that year.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּאַכַּתִּי יוֹם אֶחָד הוּא דְּעָיֵיל בַּשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: since it was still only one day that had entered into the year,
and yet it calls it a year,
learn from this:
one day in a year is considered a year.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: מִדְּאַכַּתִּי יוֹם אֶחָד הוּא דְּעָיֵיל בַּשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי מאיר reads the verse from Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's rule that one day in a year counts as a year.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words "בְּאַחַת וְשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה" on the first day of the first month.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר reads the year differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the odd word order shows it was still counted as the 600th year. "One" only means the start of the next year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other (רבי אלעזר): If it had written "in the six hundred and one year," it would be as you said. But now that it writes "in the one and six hundred year," the word "year" goes on "six hundred." And what does "one" mean? It means the beginning of one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר rejects רבי מאיר's reading of the פסוק. He explains the words a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts "one" before "six hundred" and attaches "year" to "six hundred." So the year being counted is still the 600th. The word "one" only says the next year was just beginning, not that it already counts as a full year.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר does not reject the idea of a partial year counting. He only says this specific פסוק does not teach that one DAY counts as a year.

phrases.english: And the other one:

phrases.aramaic: אִי כְּתִיב בְּ״שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת וְאַחַת שָׁנָה״ —
phrases.english: If it had written "in the six hundred and one year" —
it would be as you said.
Now that it is written "in the one and six hundred year,"
"year" goes on "six hundred."
phrases.notes: It is still counted as the 600th year.

phrases.english: And what is "one"?
It means the beginning of one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ: אִי כְּתִיב בְּשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת וְאַחַת שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי מאיר's reading from Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the word "שָׁנָה".
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word order attaches "year" to "six hundred," so "one" means only the start of the new year.

steps.title: What is רבי אלעזר's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי אלעזר learns that thirty days count as a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי אלעזר's own source. It is setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We saw why רבי אלעזר does not accept רבי מאיר's reading. But we still need to know how he learns his own rule of thirty days.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar, what is his reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבי מאיר's reading, asks for רבי אלעזר's positive source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי אלעזר's rule that thirty days count as a year.

steps.title: One day in a month counts as a month
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק calls the first day of the month "the first month," so one day in a month counts as a month.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "In the first month, on the first of the month." Since only one day had entered the month and it already calls it a month, learn from this that one day in a month counts as a month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers. רבי אלעזר learns from the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר moves the proof from the year to the month. On day one of the month, the פסוק already calls it "the first month." So one day in a month counts as a whole month.

phrases.english: As it is written: "In the first month, on the first of the month,"

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּאַכַּתִּי יוֹם אֶחָד הוּא דְּעָיֵיל בַּחֹדֶשׁ
phrases.english: since it was still only one day that had entered into the month,
and yet it calls it a month —
learn from this:
one day in a month is considered a month.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase "בָּרִאשׁוֹן בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ" teaches that one day in a month counts as a month.

steps.title: Thirty days count as a year
steps.stepSummary: A day is the unit of a month, and a month is the unit of a year. So one month (thirty days) in a year counts as a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since one day in a month counts as a month, thirty days in a year count as a year. A month goes by its units, and a year goes by its units.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי אלעזר's reasoning. It applies the month rule to the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A month is counted in days, so one unit (a day) counts as the whole month. A year is counted in months, so one unit (a month, thirty days) counts as the whole year. This is the source for רבי אלעזר's thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: According to its units (its counting units)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר says one day in a year counts as a year. רבי אלעזר says thirty days count as a year, because one unit counts as the whole. For a month the unit is a day, and for a year the unit is a month.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for רבי אלעזר's rule of how much of a year counts as a year, for example for ערלה. It explains the extra thirty days that רב נחמן adds on top of the rooting time.

phrases.english: And since one day in a month is considered a month —
thirty days in a year are considered a year.
A month goes by its units, and a year goes by its units.
phrases.notes: A month's unit is a day, and a year's unit is a month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends Step 14 from month to year.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי אלעזר, one unit counts as the whole: one day counts as a month, and thirty days (one month) count as a year.

steps.title: Both opinions hold the world was created in ניסן
steps.stepSummary: From the way רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר read the פסוק about נח, we can infer that both hold the world was created in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can learn from this that both of them hold that the world was created in ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the whole נח discussion. Both רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר hold that the world was created in ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the first day of the first month (ניסן) the start of the 601st year of נח's life. These years are counted from the month the world was created. If that were תשרי, the new year would already have begun six months earlier, in תשרי. So the counting must start in ניסן, which means the world was created in ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference / we can learn from this
The month of Nisan, the first month counting from the Exodus

steps.whyThisMatters: This inference opens the famous question of whether the world was created in ניסן or תשרי. The ברייתא that comes next continues that question.

phrases.english: By inference, both of them
phrases.notes: Both here means רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר from the previous steps.

phrases.english: hold that in Nisan the world was created.
phrases.notes: This is why the year of the world turns over in ניסן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a broader implication from the shared assumption in the reading of the נח פסוקים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר hold that the world was created in ניסן.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the world was created in תשרי, plus other key dates
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר. He says the world was created in תשרי, and the אבות were born and died in תשרי. יצחק was born on פסח. שרה, רחל, and חנה were remembered on ראש השנה, and יוסף left prison on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says the world was created in תשרי. The אבות were born in תשרי, and the אבות died in תשרי. יצחק was born on פסח. On ראש השנה, שרה, רחל, and חנה were remembered by ה׳, and it was decreed that they would conceive. On ראש השנה, יוסף came out of prison.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that this question is a real argument among the תנאים. רבי אליעזר holds that the world was created in תשרי, not ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we only saw the view that the world was created in ניסן. Now רבי אליעזר gives the opposite view and attaches a list of great events to תשרי and ראש השנה. The ברייתא continues on the next דף, where רבי יהושע argues and says ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of Tishrei, the month of ראש השנה
The Patriarchs: אברהם, יצחק, and יעקב
Was remembered by ה׳, meaning she was granted a child

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי אליעזר (with a yud, the one speaking here) with רבי אלעזר from the previous steps. They are different people. רבי אלעזר holds ניסן, and רבי אליעזר holds תשרי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument about when the world was created comes up across ש״ס. It also explains why ראש השנה in תשרי is the day of judgment and of remembrance.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer says:
In Tishrei the world was created;
phrases.notes: This is the opposite of what the גמרא just worked out in the previous step.

phrases.english: in Tishrei the Patriarchs were born;
in Tishrei the Patriarchs died;
on Passover Isaac was born;
phrases.notes: יצחק is the exception to the other אבות. He was born on פסח.

phrases.english: on Rosh HaShana were remembered
Sarah, Rachel, and Hannah;
phrases.notes: ה׳ remembered them on ראש השנה: it was decreed then that each of them, childless until then, would conceive.

phrases.english: on Rosh HaShana Joseph came out
from prison;
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next דף.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: בְּתִשְׁרִי נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the ניסן view inferred in step 16 is disputed among the תנאים, beginning with רבי אליעזר's opposing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: the world was created in תשרי. The אבות were born and died in תשרי, יצחק was born on פסח, שרה, רחל, and חנה were remembered on ראש השנה, and יוסף left prison on ראש השנה.
